title: Senior Engineering Manager
description:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London or Remote (UK) | 💰 £138,000 - £175,000 + Equity + Benefits

About the Role

This role is for a Senior Engineering Manager where you’ll be a manager of managers. You will be leading across multiple teams in an org of around 20-30 people. We’re expanding and your role as the Senior EM will be to grow and build new squads as needed. Your direct reports will include Tech Leads, Senior Engineers and 2-3 Engineering Managers.

Senior Engineering Managers at Monzo are part of cross-functional, autonomous teams and groups. Our teams are mission driven, and typically include Product Managers, backend, web and mobile engineers as well as data scientists, designers and subject matter experts relevant to that mission. Teams are organised into groups, and then collectives - we aim to keep our line management structure as shallow as possible, and for teams to directly own decision making relevant to their work.

Senior Engineering Managers are accountable for the technical and delivery outcomes for their area - that means supporting and developing best in class engineering talent, as well as creating an inclusive team environment for people to do their best work. You’ll be responsible for structuring, organising, supporting and challenging your team to deliver on their mission.

You can read more on the expectations of Senior Engineering Managers in our Progression Framework.

Is this role right for you?

While this is not a role which requires hands-on-coding, we are looking for an experienced manager who has a strong technical and delivery background and has worked as a software engineer in previous roles.

We recognise that Senior Engineering Managers lead in different ways, we’re looking for someone who is adept at:

  • Delivery and Execution: Enjoys taking accountability for delivery across your squad(s), collaborating with the Technical Lead and Product Manager.
  • Engineering and Operational Excellence: Actively fosters a high bar for engineering excellence within your teams. You’re accountable for the technical outcomes your teams deliver alongside individual engineer performance and growth, so holding a high bar (and clearly articulating your expectations) is key.
  • People Leadership: Has experience directly managing at least 2-3 Engineering Managers and leading orgs of around ~20 engineers. You can support, coach and develop them through their career with regular 1:1s and continuous feedback.
  • Technical Influence: Partners with senior engineers to drive technical initiatives that raise the bar for our engineering practices.
  • Stakeholder Relationships: Builds strong stakeholder relationships with other teams, and creates a focus space for engineers to do their best work.
  • Organisational Wide Impact: Collaborates with the wider engineering organisation to contribute to company-wide best managerial and technical practices and standards.

We consider your application across all open EM roles at Monzo independent of which role you've applied for, so if you've recently applied to a similar role at Monzo and have been unsuccessful, please wait 6 months before applying again.

How we work 💻:

Locations & Flexible Working :

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles.

We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance.

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

The interview process:

After an initial informal recruiter call you go through two main stages

  1. Initial Call (1 hour) You'll meet with one of our Senior Engineering Managers or Engineering Directors. They'll ask you about your previous experience, in particular people leadership, product delivery and technical leadership. They’ll ask example based questions (‘Tell me about a time when…’)
  2. Loop Stage (3 hours 30 mins) The Loop stage consists of 3 x 60 min interviews that take place over 1-2 days (depending on your availability) and one 30 minute reverse interview (more details below).

The Loop is one stage and the interviews in this stage are:

- Team and Org Management (1 hour)
An example based interview with 1-2 of our engineering leaders. They’re interested to hear examples from your previous experience on the teams you’ve led, how you’ve shaped and partnered with product, and the impact you had.

- System Design (1 hour)
You'll partner with a Staff or Principal Engineer on a technical whiteboarding exercise.

- Behavioural (1 hour)
Similar to Team and Org Management, this is an example based interview with 1-2 Engineering Leaders. This interview focuses on your people leadership style and core behaviours as an Engineering Manager.

- Chat with an Engineering Leader (30 mins)
At Monzo, we believe interviews are a two-way street. This will be your opportunity to ask us any questions about Monzo, engineering leadership or our teams – whatever’s on your mind.

All things going well, you'll have completed the hiring process 🚀

Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You’ll have the chance to speak to our recruitment team throughout the process.

What’s in it for you:

💰 £138,000 - £175,000 + Equity + Benefits

✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK

✅ We can sponsor visas

📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.

📚Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences

➕And much more, see our full list of benefits here

#LI-Remote #LI-AL1

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog, 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊

description:
Sprowston Community Academy and Sixth Form

Cannerby Lane

Sprowston

Norwich

NR7 8NE

Vacancy

Teacher of MFL

Salary MPS/UPS range, also suitable for ECT

1 FTE

To commence April 2027 (an earlier start may be accommodated)

“Being the best version of Sprowston that we can be”

We are looking to appoint a passionate and creative teacher of Modern Foreign Languages. Ideally applicants will have a specialism in Spanish but an ability to also teach other languages would be valued. We currently offer languages to GCSE level but with sufficient student interest we would be willing to offer A level provision in the future.

The successful candidate will be passionate about languages and committed to teaching students of all abilities. We want to inspire and engage students so that they enjoy learning a modern foreign language and see it as a relevant and valuable skill in the world that we live in. We are particularly keen to encourage more students to choose to study languages to GCSE level and including A level. We are keen to further promote international dimension and to encourage our students to see themselves as part of a global community. An ability to offer a contribution to this aspect of student's personal development would be an asset in this role as would be any contribution to the wider promotion of languages or contribution to the life of the school.

Sprowston Community Academy is a growing 11-18 school. We are exceptionally proud of the journey that we are on and the provision that we offer young people. Our ethos is focused on high expectations for academic development, behaviour and personal development. We believe that strong relationships are at the heart of our school and inclusion runs through everything that we do.

Ofsted 2026 said “Leaders place a strong emphasis on staff wellbeing and workload, contributing to high levels of staff morale and a positive working culture. Staff feel respected, valued and supported. They have a shared identity and pride in the school”.

This role would be suitable for an Early Career Teacher. We are committed to providing high quality support and CPD and the successful applicant will join a team that is extremely welcoming, collaborative and supportive.

We reserve the right to close these vacancies early if sufficient applications are received and therefore early application is encouraged.

We are currently unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must have an existing right to work in the UK.

For further information about Sprowston Community Academy please visit the website sprowstoncommunityacademy.co.uk

To apply please select the ‘Apply now’ button and enter your details.

Please include in the personal statement section of your application why you believe you are suitable for this role in terms of skill, experience and personal qualities.

You must “Submit” your fully completed application by the closing date/time.

Closing date: Wednesday 9 December 2026 at 9.00am
Interviews: Week commencing 14 December 2026

Broad Horizons Education Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. This post is likely to come under the requirements of the Childcare (Disqualification) 2009 Regulations, therefore successful candidates will be required to complete a declaration form to establish whether they are disqualified under these regulations. Applicants must be prepared to undertake an Enhanced DBS check. Right to Work in the UK will need to be established. We are an equal opportunities employer.

title: Senior Sales Development Representative - 4 Day Week + Remote
description:
Still get a buzz from a cold call? Good. So do we.

Our SDRs call commercial, project and operations leaders at some of the UK's biggest construction firms. They're busy, they're blunt, and they've heard every software pitch going (some of them twice before lunch). Earn their two minutes, find a genuine problem on a live project, and you'll hand over a meeting your Account Executive can actually win.

You've done this before, so you know a full calendar isn't the same as a good one. Here, quality wins every time, and you'll have a playbook that works, coaching from people who know construction, and a team that backs you to do it properly.

If you want your experience to count for more than your dial count, keep reading.

(this will be a long write up but we like to give you all the details before you spend your time applying)

_________________________________________________________________________________________

We are Shape.Construction!

We are digitising the largest and most fundamental industry in the world, the industry that literally builds the foundations of the civilisation we all depend on to spare us from a brutal hunter-gatherer life: CONSTRUCTION

It is one of the least digitised industries in the world but also the largest – 1 in 9 people globally work in the construction industry and it constitutes 11% of global GDP.

Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Watch our short film about it).

We got our start as a high-end construction project management consultancy. As a consultancy, we are focused on genuinely upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. We then take the deep understanding of the projects we work on to develop construction management software products that anyone can use to deliver their projects better.

We are building a full suite of products one module at a time – kind of like office 365 but for construction management - Check out Shape, our construction management tech

The core of all this is our true secret sauce; people. We only recruit the very best both in capability and personality. We are deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that is optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People that join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined.

This approach has allowed us to grow from just 2 people in 2017 to over 220 today (including consultancy) and we are still very much at the beginning! Joining us isn't just some "job", it is a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life.

4 core values for a good life

We believe a life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships with others and challenging yourself to create a positive impact. So our values reflect the 4 levels of relationships that each of us has:

  • Grow yourself – Your relationship with yourself
  • Care about people – Your relationship with others around you
  • Execute to greatness – Your relationship with your team
  • Build civilisation – Your relationship with humanity and the world

This goes much deeper but for the sake of brevity, we will keep the summary version!

We enshrined our values in our vision

We exist so that everyone in our team can thrive in a high-impact community that:

  • Connects us with meaningful relationships
  • Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans
  • Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures

We believe that, by first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.

And enable the achievement of our vision through our dual missions:

  1. To fully digitise the construction of human civilisation
  2. To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society

_________________________________________________________________________________________

The Role

Purpose of the role

You're where every Shape deal starts, and one of the people who sets the standard for how we prospect. As you grow, you'll shape our messaging and set the bar for the SDRs who join after you.

What the job actually is

You know the job. Most of your day is on the phone, and you'll hear "no", "not now" and "just send me an email" more than anything else. Here, you'll be calling commercial, project and operations leaders at tier 1 and tier 2 construction firms (main contractors and the subcontractors who work for them). They're running live projects, their time is precious and they're wary of anyone selling software. Almost all of our pipeline is outbound, apart from customer referrals, so the meetings you book are ones you've created yourself.

You also know that to be good at cold calling, you have to genuinely love it. If you don't, and you plan to go through the motions, it's a boring job, and it shows on every call. We're looking for someone who still gets a buzz from turning a cold "who's this?" into a real conversation.

Quality over quantity, always. We care about the work we do and take pride in doing it properly, and we want people who feel the same. You'll know a booked meeting isn't the same as a good one. Here, it means understanding their problem properly: being curious enough to ask the second and third question, listening more than you talk, and knowing by the end of the call what's actually going wrong for them, on which project, and why it matters now. It also means only offering a solution to people who genuinely want or need to fix it. If they don't, you thank them and move on. Get that right and the meeting follows naturally, and it's one worth having.

How the team is set up

You'll sit in the UK sales team, working day to day with an Account Executive who takes your meetings forward to a free launch and then a contract. You open the door, they win the deal, and you succeed together. You'll work with a CRM, a dialler and call recording, plus a playbook, a library of calls that have actually won, and AI call-prep tools built for how we sell.

Where you'll work

Remote, anywhere in the UK, with the chance to attend industry events in person in the near future.

Why it's worth it

  • A career in a market that's only just going digital: around $10 trillion is spent on construction every year, yet it's one of the least digitised industries in the world, and spending on construction management software is forecast to nearly double by 2030. People who can sell software and genuinely understand construction are rare. Learn both here, and you'll have skills that stay in demand for years as the industry catches up, and you'll be helping it work better along the way.
  • Senior conversations from the start: you'll be speaking directly to leaders at some of the UK's biggest construction firms, not working your way through gatekeepers.
  • Coaching that knows the industry: weekly reviews and coaching from people who've lived and breathed construction, on site, not just on the phones.
  • A playbook that works: built from calls that have won, so you're not starting from scratch.
  • Progression on merit: a proper conversation about your next step within a year, based on what you've shown.
  • You'll shape how we sell: what you learn and suggest makes it into the playbook.
  • A 4-day week: the same standards and targets, delivered in four days.

Your top responsibilities

  • Open doors: start proper conversations, every day, with the people who feel the problem and can decide.
  • Qualify properly: test the problem early, dig in before you pitch, and keep qualifying after the "yes".
  • Hand over cleanly: your CRM notes tell the story, so your Account Executive picks up exactly where you left off.
  • Be obsessed with your numbers: know them every day, track them weekly and act on what they tell you.
  • Raise the bar: once you're up to speed, share what's working, contribute to the playbook and help newer SDRs get better faster.

Your roadmap: your first 30 days and beyond

You bring the experience. We'll make sure you're selling the Shape way, with confidence, by week 3 or 4.

  • Before day 1, ready to go: your CRM, dialler, call recording and your own Shape login set up, so week 1 is spent learning.
  • Week 1, understand the why: the problems we solve, who for, and why it beats how contractors work today, with the product shown in action by Customer Success.
  • Week 2, build your pitch: write your first-call pitch, compare it with the winning calls in our library, get it reviewed, and make your first live calls if you're ready.
  • Weeks 3–4, up and running: calling daily with call reviews, booking your first meetings and handing them over properly.
  • By day 30: signed off as ready to call, every call in the library listened to, and your first measures reviewed with your manager.
  • Months 2–3, ramp: half the full target, with your own quality scorecard.
  • By the end of month 3, full target: the same target every SDR carries, in line with your probation period.
  • 6–12 months, step up: own a set of key accounts or a segment, help refine our messaging and set the bar for newer SDRs, with a clear path to Account Executive or SDR Team Lead.

Why three months is realistic: it's quick by industry standards, and that's deliberate. You won't be figuring it out alone. You'll have a playbook built from calls that have won, regular call reviews, weekly 1:1s and your own scorecard. Our best have been fully up to speed in a month. Training never stops at day 30, however experienced you are.

How you'll be measured

Good numbers come from good conversations. You'll have your own monthly scorecard, built around three questions: are you reaching the right people, are those calls turning into real conversations, and are those conversations turning into meetings worth having?

Your main target is qualified meetings attended: meetings that actually take place, where your Account Executive agrees there's a genuine opportunity. You'll know your numbers from day one, and we'll go through them with you every week.

No grey areas: you and your Account Executive are partners. What makes a meeting qualified is written down and shared, so you'll both know where the bar is. If you ever see one differently, you talk it through with the call recording in front of you. Decisions come down to facts, never opinion or politics.

What our best are doing: booking

title: Teacher of Music
description:
Job Title: Teacher of Music 

Actual Annual Salary: £34,069 - £52,835 (M1 to UPS3 based on 1.0 FTE) 

Contract Type: Permanent 

Hours: Full-time, 32.5 hours per week, 1.0 FTE 

Provisional Start Date: 12 April 2027 

We are seeking an inspirational and talented Teacher of Music with a passion for delivering exceptional educational experiences and fostering a lifelong love of music in young people. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in developing students' musical knowledge, creativity, confidence, and performance skills, while contributing to a vibrant and ambitious school community. Our commitment to high expectations, excellent teaching, and a rich, contemporary curriculum enables us to create opportunities for every student to thrive and succeed. 

The successful candidate will be required to teach BTEC Level 2 Music at Key Stage 4.

About you: 

You will be: 

  • a qualified teacher or hold an equivalent teaching qualification.  
  • able to deliver the curriculum in your chosen area and consistently teach high quality lessons across relevant key stages. 
  • a strong communicator with the ability to embrace change, motivate colleagues and build positive relationships with students, staff and parents.

title: Community Lead & Talent Acquisition Advisor - EMEA
description:
Hi, I’m Kayla :) I lead global community activation within Partnerships at Ashby. Before joining a year ago, I spent 15 years in TA and was an Ashby customer. I made the move out of TA into this role, and nothing I’d learned has gone to waste. If anything, I’ve learnt even more from the community. It’s genuinely one of the most rewarding and fun roles I’ve had, and as I step into a leadership role, I’m on the hunt for someone to take over the work in EMEA and evolve it further.

We’re hiring an experienced TA Expert & Community Lead to grow one of our most successful GTM experiments: a high-touch, customer-led approach to growth. The model is already working in EMEA, built on curated events, product education and early community activation. You’ll own it across our target markets (UK&I, France, Nordics and Benelux), from customer breakfasts and curated experiences to enablement sessions and product demos.

This role suits someone who has worked with Ashby All-in-One, has a solid background in TA, and cares about tools, process, hospitality and community building. It also works well for TA people who still love the work but want to use what they know somewhere new. You’ll work closely with Sales, CS and Product Marketing, own a region end-to-end, and see how community connects to pipeline and retention.

A quick summary on travel, since it’s usually the first question and we know it means time away from home: you’ll have events in London regularly, plus one trip to another EMEA city a month, usually for around four days. Busier periods can mean two trips abroad in a month. There is flex, though. I’m a mum of three, and in this role, I’ve been able to stay home and take meaningful time off during every school holiday. We plan the calendar well in advance, so you’ll know what’s coming and can sort things at home with plenty of notice.

It’s also one of the best parts of the job. I’ve met some amazing people and had some really cool experiences along the way, from hosting a dinner cruise on the Seine and a TA leader workshop with a partner at the Shangri-La Paris, to spending time in customers’ offices in Stockholm, our company offsite in Playa Del Carmen, and hosting the mainstage at our first Ashby One London.

What you’ll do

  • Lead EMEA Community Events

    • Run community events across target EMEA markets. Event types might include:

      • Customer learning breakfasts

      • A mixed ecosystem event for customers and prospects

      • Partner cocktail events or roundtables co-hosted with local ecosystem players

    • Build and nurture relationships with TA leaders

    • Partner with Event Ops on venue selection, invites, and post-event recaps

    • Drive improvement and reimagine how we can show up in a very meaningful way for the community

  • Drive Customer Education

    • Become an Expert in Ashby + TA leader needs to curate relevant content

    • Design and lead live sessions that help customers activate key Ashby features and keep customers ahead on key TA trends and topics

    • Partner with CS and Product Marketing teams on the Ashby Hidden Gems program

    • Develop and distribute product tips, dashboards, and templates to increase customer sophistication

  • Expand EMEA Community and Customer Advocacy

    • Help Ashby deepen its brand and trust by showing up consistently and thoughtfully

    • Participate in and help advise on content for ACE (Ashby Customer Expert) events when we bring the program to EMEA

    • Partner with GTM teams on prospect and customer onsite visits

    • Moderate panels, attend events, and build a presence at industry gatherings

Who you’ll work with

You’ll report directly to me, but work closely with myself and Willem, who has pioneered what community growth looks like at Ashby. Within partnerships, you’ll also work closely with Katie to scale trusted community partner relationships and Louise to bring Owned Community experiences, like Ashby Cafe, to life. You’ll also partner day to day with our EMEA Sales and CS teams, who know our customers and prospects best and help shape who we bring into the room.

About You

We think the ideal person for this role will have experience and skills that look something like this:

  • You’ve been an Ashby power user or at least very familiar with Ashby and seen its benefits first-hand—someone who knows the product and Ashby community, champions good recruiting practices, and isn’t afraid to dive into dashboards, workflows, or templates

  • You’ve built a reputation inside organizations as the go-to expert on TA process and tooling

  • You’re a strong communicator—whether facilitating a breakfast, writing a post-event summary, or helping a customer understand how to build a dashboard

  • You love curating and connecting people and ideas. You get energy from hosting, matchmaking, and finding smart formats to share what works

  • You’re excited about being on the road ~2x/month and tapping into your existing network (and growing it!) in the TA space

  • You have strong business acumen. You understand how community supports the wider business and work well with Sales and CS to make sure our programs are reaching the right people

  • You’re entrepreneurial and experimental in nature. You’re not looking for rigid playbooks; you want room to try new formats and evolve what ‘great’ looks like. You come prepared with AI tools / automations that help us execute faster while maintaining quality.

  • You believe in unreasonable hospitality—the idea that going above and beyond for a customer doesn’t just build goodwill, it builds momentum.

This Role Probably Isn't Right If ...

  • You’re not excited about hosting or don’t enjoy the details of curating small, thoughtful gatherings

  • You hate writing and have difficulty building a cohesive brief (this is a very important skill at Ashby)

  • You don’t enjoy travelling and building new connections while you’re at it

  • You’ve never had hands-on TA experience

  • You’ve never used Ashby and aren’t familiar with modern TA systems and practices

  • You prefer working from a very established playbook and are uncomfortable with ambiguity or iteration

  • You’re uncomfortable with moderating discussions or being a speaker

  • You’d rather focus purely on the community side and aren’t keen to understand how it connects to the wider business

  • You only have an ‘events background’. For this role, we need folks with deep knowledge of the TA ecosystem and a proven network in major city hubs such as London, Paris, Berlin, Stockholm and Amsterdam.

Interview Plan

  • Recruiter Screen with Kayla/Willem - 30 minutes

  • Hiring Manager Interview with Kayla - 45 minutes

  • Cross-functional Panel - 1 hour

  • Assignment (written) - 2 hours

    • Followed by Assignment Review with Kayla - 30 Minutes

  • Final Round - 1-1.5 hours

Benefits

  • Compelling benefits offerings, location dependent

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

 About the Job:

 Teams are putting AI agents into production everywhere, and almost no one owns controlling them once they’re there. Agents make decisions at runtime, change behavior with every model update, and touch systems that were never designed for them. The teams that figure out how to govern, observe, and control agents in production will set the pace for the AI era. That’s the category we’re building.

 LaunchDarkly is hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the story and go-to-market for how teams govern, observe, and control AI agents in production, a new capability within the LaunchDarkly platform. You’ll set the strategy, build the story, and be judged on pipeline and revenue, not assets shipped. You’ll work with Product and Demand Gen on go-to-market strategy, with Sales on live deals, with RevOps on pricing and packaging, and with partners and analysts on defining the category. It’s early, it’s moving fast, and you’ll have real ownership.

 This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates with minimal direction. You’ll thrive here if you’re data-oriented and a GTM operator at heart: curious about what’s happening in the market, quick to dig into the numbers, and able to identify and size new opportunities before anyone asks. You’d rather connect what product, sales, and marketing are each seeing into one strategic direction than optimize one part of the business, and you want to be measured on business outcomes, not deliverables.

 Responsibilities:

• Own the go-to-market plan for agent management — know what’s happening in the business and the market, build and deliver the GTM plan against company goals, and align product, sales, and marketing leaders behind it. Bring GTM input and recommendations into quarterly and annual planning.

• Build the category narrative — define the audience, positioning, and differentiation for agent management with product and PMM leadership, grounded in customer and market research. Differentiate against observability, LLMOps, and agent-framework vendors, and adapt the narrative across web, content, and sales conversations.

• Lead go-to-market for launches — define the story, audience, and launch plan for releases, events, and customer stories, and work with cross-functional partners so each ships with a clear message and enabled field teams.

• Enable sales to win — work with sales leaders and reps to build what they need, from enablement and discovery guidance to outbound messaging and competitive positioning. Track win-rate impact, and support strategic deals where the narrative is decisive.

• Optimize the customer journey — partner with marketing, sales development, sales, and customer success to find where buyers stall from first touch to closed-won, and recommend and implement fixes that improve conversion, velocity, and deal quality.

• Experiment and adapt the GTM plan — build a clear view of how agent management is performing, monitor market and funnel data, run tests with marketing and sales across audiences, messaging, and channels, and use customer conversations and win/loss analysis to decide what to scale, change, or stop.

• Be the voice of the market — share customer, field, and data insights with product and marketing leadership to inform roadmap, pricing and packaging, and investment decisions. Brief analysts on agent management, and report on GTM progress and outcomes.

 Qualifications:

• 8+ years in product marketing or a related GTM role at B2B software companies, including owning go-to-market for a segment or product tried to growth targets

• A track record of impact you can quantify: pipeline you built, win rate you moved, or revenue that grew because of work you led

• Fluency with technical buyers (developers, engineering leaders, AI teams) and the depth to hold your own with product managers and sales engineers

• Comfort in the data: you can read a funnel, find where it breaks, and turn that into a decision

• Strong writing and a high bar for quality, with examples that drove measurable business outcomes

• A history of building trust fast with sales and product, and influencing leaders without owning their teams

• Low ego and team-first: you care about the outcome more than the credit, and you step in where the team needs you

• Bonus:

• Experience marketing AI infrastructure, LLMOps, or agent tooling, or deep familiarity with the observability and DevOps categories we compete with

• Hands-on experience building AI-powered workflows

 Pay:

 Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 4:

• Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $156,700 - $215,490 **

• Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $141,000 - $193,930 **

 LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

 *Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.

 About LaunchDarkly:

 Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.

 The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

• Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages

 LaunchDarkly is seeking an Executive Assistant to partner closely with our Chief Revenue Officer and support the broader global Revenue organization as it scales.

As the organization grows, the EA may also provide administrative support to other senior Revenue leaders. The right person will be comfortable working across time zones, navigating senior stakeholders, handling confidential information, and learning the CRO’s priorities and working style.

Software powers the world and LaunchDarkly empowers all teams to deliver and control their software.

• Manage the CRO’s calendar, priorities, meeting flow, and time allocation across a globally distributed organization.

• Triage scheduling requests and prepare the CRO for key meetings by confirming logistics, participants, and materials; recommend what should be delegated, deferred, or declined.

• Manage domestic and international travel, bookings, logistics, expenses, approvals, and last-minute changes.

• Plan and coordinate Revenue leadership offsites, including quarterly gatherings, and other executive events; attend select events in person.

title: Director, Engineering
description:
Headquarters: Remote UK, Remote Canada, Remote US

 CircleCI is the platform that powers continuous integration and delivery for the world's best engineering teams — helping them build, test, and ship software quickly, safely, and confidently, including the new generation of AI-assisted development. Do you want to lead the teams that set that example for customers?

 The Director, Engineering is a strategic leader who directs operational units across the engineering organization. You will own the technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for your engineering organization (typically 4-5 teams including engineering managers), collaborating on organizational engineering strategy and partnering across functions to deliver measurable business impact.

 This is a broad, high-impact seat — you'll partner closely with the VP of Engineering and peer leaders across the org to shape structure, roadmap, and operating standards for a group that's growing and evolving fast.

 This role balances technical depth with strategic thinking, people development with execution, and short-term delivery with long-term sustainability. You will work with Product, Go-to-Market teams, customers, and executive leadership to drive CircleCI's mission forward.

 Strategic Planning

 Your Strategic Responsibilities:

• Lead and grow a multi-team engineering organization, with ownership of its structure, headcount, and provide input for product strategy

• Partner with the VP of Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders on technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for your organization, ensuring alignment with company objectives.

• Raise the bar on engineering practices, operating standards, and delivery quality across the group

• Build and develop a strong management layer — hiring, coaching, and growing engineering managers and leads

• Define operating metrics and team goals; craft strategies to scale infrastructure and meet business objectives

• Cultivate a culture of excellence that closes the gap between business/roadmap commitments and what gets delivered

• Lead distributed engineering teams to deliver highly available, highly secure experiences at scale

• Bring real AI competency to the role — not just personal use of AI tools, but building the systems and practices that let your teams get genuine leverage from AI

• Represent your organization's roadmap, tradeoffs, and constraints clearly to Product and other cross-functional partners

 Your Decision-Making Authority:

 You have full authority to:

• Hire, promote, and performance-manage all engineers and managers within your organization

• Make final decisions on administrative and operational matters within your domain

• Approve technical architecture decisions that impact your organization alongside highly experienced senior engineers

• Prioritize and sequence engineering work; allocate budget for team tools, training, and resources

• Represent engineering in cross-functional forums and make commitments on behalf of your organization

 What We're Looking For

 This is a key role with significant impact on CircleCI's engineering organization and business outcomes.

• 5+ years in engineering leadership, including direct management of managers

• Ability to translate business objectives into technical strategy and enable teams to deliver reliable, resilient, and secure features at scale

• A proven track record of building strong, aligned teams across varied technical surfaces

• Thorough understanding of developer tools market, practices, competition, and trends

• Genuine fluency with AI-assisted engineering workflows and what it takes to operationalize them at a team level

• Expert manager with ability to mentor and develop individual contributors and managers; build high-performing teams through recruiting, coaching, and creating growth opportunities

• Drive frameworks for people development, performance, inclusion, and belonging across your organization

• Data-driven problem solver who handles risk and uncertainty; coordinates work spanning departments with alignment to organizational goals

• Strong verbal and written communication skills; ability to influence teams, peers, leaders, executives, and customers

• Comfortable working with globally distributed teams across multiple time zones using synchronous and asynchronous communication, and making hard structural and personnel calls, not just process improvements

 $215,000 — $295,000 CAD

 About CircleCI

 CircleCI is the world’s largest continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform, and the hub where code moves from idea to delivery. As one of the most-used DevOps tools - processing more than 3 million jobs a day - CircleCI has unique access to data on how the most effective engineering teams work, and the tools to help software companies successfully leverage the power of AI into their commercial applications. title: Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Trust
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

 Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

 The Community You Will Join:

 Everyone at Airbnb thinks about trust, but our team obsesses over it daily. At the core of trust is safety, and thus we spend a significant amount of our time and energy keeping the community safe. The Trust team is responsible for developing the technology that helps protect our community and platform from fraud while also ensuring our hosts, guests, homes, and experiences meet our high standards. We constantly work to fight against online fraud (such as monetary loss, compromised accounts, spam and scam in messages, fake inventory, etc.) as well as offline fraud (theft, property damage, personal safety, etc.). We also work on onboarding and screening of users, and think about complex topics like identity and reputation to ensure that every interaction with Airbnb helps build trust in us and our community. Trust Engineering is responsible for the technology vision and development of a complex stack that runs on every key interaction on the platform. Trust Engineering is at the forefront of AI and ML innovation, helping develop novel techniques and advancing the state-of-art in Machine Learning to continually build and maintain trust across our platform.

 The Difference You Will Make:

 As a senior technical individual contributor, you will partner closely with our leaders across the broader technical organization helping design, execute and deliver in a complex and collaborative roadmap of Trust engineering efforts that will require collaboration across many parts of the organization and many parts of Airbnb. Although you will be at one of our highest levels of seniority, all individual contributors at Airbnb are Software Engineers which means we expect you to be hands on and contribute code.

 A Typical day:

• Define and execute on the long-term ML technical vision and strategy for the Trust organization, identifying key investments, architecting scalable solutions, and championing best practices that advance the state-of-the-art in production ML systems.

• Serve as a technical leader and mentor to other ML and software engineers across the organization, providing guidance on complex architectural and modeling challenges, and raising the overall technical bar.

• Drive and deliver large-scale, multi-quarter ML initiatives that span multiple teams, influencing roadmaps and ensuring alignment between platform and product

• Work with large scale structured and unstructured data, build and continuously improve cutting edge Machine Learning models for Airbnb product, business and operational use cases.

• Work collaboratively with cross-functional partners including software engineers, product managers, operations and data scientists, identify opportunities for business impact, understand, refine, and prioritize requirements for machine learning models, drive engineering decisions, and quantify impact.

• Work closely with other trust defense and platform teams to tackle the changing landscape of fraud attacks.

• Hands-on develop, productionize, and operate Machine Learning models and pipelines at scale, including both batch and real-time use cases.

• Examples include: Anomaly detection models, ML models for continuous risk evaluation, Multimodality and Agentic AI

 Your Expertise:

• 12+ years of industry experience in applied Machine Learning

• 2-3+ years working with LLMs and novel GenAI technologies. Proficiency and proven experience on Agentic AI (frameworks, orchestration, architecture and productionization).

• A Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in CS/ML or related field

• Strong programming (Scala / Python / Java/ C++ or equivalent) and data engineering skills

• Deep understanding of Machine Learning best practices (eg. training/serving skew minimization, A/B test, feature engineering, feature/model selection), algorithms (eg. gradient boosted trees, neural networks/deep learning, optimization) and domains (eg. genAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, computer vision, personalization and recommendation, anomaly detection)

• Experience with these technologies: AgenticAI, Tensorflow, PyTorch, Kubernetes,

• Industry experience building end-to-end Machine Learning and Agentic infrastructure and/or building and productionizing Machine Learning models

• Exposure to architectural patterns of a large, high-scale software applications (e.g., well-designed APIs, high volume data pipelines, efficient algorithms, models)

• Experience with test driven development, familiar with A/B testing, incremental delivery and deployment.

• Experience with the Trust and Risk domain is a plus.

 Your Location:

 This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

 Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

 Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

 We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com . Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

 We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

 Equal Employment Opportunity :

 Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Airbnb are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.
 How We'll Take Care of You:

 Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.

A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @ airbnb.com or @ ext.airbnb.com email addresses. You will take those recommendations and drive them to realization: building the plan, aligning the stakeholders, and landing the change across Product, Sales, Finance, Marketing, Legal, Billing, and Operations.

 You will work with guidance from the Sr. Director of Pricing & Packaging, but you will own the execution of your programs end to end. You will keep multiple initiatives moving at once, adapt quickly as priorities shift, and make sure that what we decide in the pricing team is what customers and the field actually experience. This is a high-impact role for someone who combines strong B2B SaaS pricing acumen with the discipline of a program and operations leader. You understand why a pricing change is the right call, and you know how to get it done.

 You will report to our Sr. Director of Packaging & Pricing, and you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is a registered employer.

 What You Will Do:

 Program execution

• Own the end-to-end execution of pricing and packaging initiatives, from the handoff of a recommendation through launch and post-launch measurement. Examples include new packaging constructs, list price changes, rate card updates, AI and new-capability monetization, and customer migrations.

• Build and manage detailed program plans, timelines, dependencies, risk registers, and RACI structures across multiple concurrent projects.

• Translate pricing recommendations into clear requirements and action plans for the teams that implement them, including Product, Engineering, Sales Ops, Finance, Billing, Legal, Marketing, and Customer Success.

• Run program cadences, including stand-ups, steering committees, and executive updates. Surface risks and decisions early, and escalate with clear options and trade-offs.

• Re-plan and re-prioritize quickly as business priorities, market conditions, and leadership direction change.

 Cross-functional leadership and communication

• Build trusted partnerships across the organization and secure stakeholder buy-in, often without direct authority.

• Write clear, executive-ready documents, including program briefs, decision memos, launch plans, FAQs, and status reports.

• Present program status, outcomes, and recommendations to senior stakeholders and leadership.

• Partner with Sales Enablement and Marketing to develop field-facing materials such as pricing guides, discounting guidelines, talk tracks, and training, so that changes are understood and adopted.

 Pricing operations and governance

• Operationalize pricing policy by partnering with the right cross-functional partners for critical changes to prices, discount guidelines, approval workflows, quoting and CPQ configuration, billing and systems changes, and exception handling.

• Contribute to pricing governance, including intake, prioritization, decision rights, approvals, and deal-desk escalation paths.

• Build repeatable playbooks, templates, and processes for pricing launches, migrations, and changes so the team can scale.

• Partner with Finance, Revenue Operations, and Business Systems to ensure pricing changes are accurately reflected in systems, reporting, and forecasts.

 Analytics and performance tracking

• Define success metrics for each program and track post-launch performance, including ARR, NRR, ARPU, attach rate, price realization, discount levels, and migration performance.

• Use data to monitor adoption, identify issues, and recommend corrective actions or follow-on work.

• Work with the pricing team to understand the research, models, and assumptions behind each recommendation so you can execute with context and flag when results diverge from the plan.

• Support competitive pricing and packaging monitoring that informs ongoing program decisions.

 You Have:

• 7 to 10+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, revenue operations, strategy and operations, program management, or a related commercial function, with at least 5 years in B2B SaaS pricing or monetization.

• A proven track record of driving pricing or packaging changes to execution in a multi-product, multi-segment SaaS business, not only recommending them. You can point to launches or migrations you delivered and the outcomes they produced.

• Strong program and project management skills. You are skilled at managing complex, cross-functional initiatives with many dependencies and stakeholders.

• Operations experience, such as pricing operations, deal desk, revenue operations, sales operations, or business operations, and familiarity with how pricing flows through quoting, billing, and finance systems.

• Strong business and pricing strategy acumen. You understand value metrics, packaging architecture, unit economics, and how pricing decisions affect revenue, margin, and customer experience.

• Excellent verbal and written communication. You can distill complex topics into clear narratives for executives, partners, and the field.

• Comfort working cross-functionally, with the ability to influence and build consensus across teams with different priorities.

• The ability to adapt and pivot quickly. You stay organized and focused as priorities change, and you bring structure to ambiguity.

• Analytical skills sufficient to size impacts and track results: advanced Excel or Sheets, working knowledge of SQL, and experience with a BI tool (e.g., Tableau).

• A collaborative, low-ego working style that fits Smartsheet's culture.

• Experience in work management, collaboration, productivity, or analytics SaaS, ideally with AI-enhanced products.

• Experience launching or operationalizing pricing for AI features.

• Exposure to PLG plus enterprise "hybrid GTM" environments.

• Experience managing customer migrations, grandfathering, or renewal-based price changes.

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

The Strategic Account Executive is a field-based position with ownership of an assigned territory in the Middle East region focused on net new logo opportunities. You will have the ability to utilize a robust internal resource model, a broad tech stack, and a global partner directory to position yourself for future success.

We will consider applicants based in the UK or France only

You will:

  • Create, implement, measure and review a personal plan that drives achievement of performance goals aligned to the regional sales strategy.

You have:

  • 6+ years quota-carrying experience selling enterprise software solutions, preferably IAM or cybersecurity
  • Demonstrable, successful experience of selling in the Middle East region
  • Proven experience of winning multiple new logo deals of $150k+ ARR and exceeding quota
  • A results-oriented mindset with proven ability to conduct effective account/territory planning & pipeline generation
  • Sustainable record of signing strategic and large projects, with long and complex sales cycles.
  • Established sector-related C level contacts.
  • Successful record dealing with strategic buyers.
  • Deep knowledge of the relevant key drivers of change in the industry.
  • Background working with regional/national/global partners and system integrators.
  • Prior training and experience in value selling and account planning methodologies.
  • Eligibility to work in the UK or France.

Life at Ping:

We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day.

  • Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone.
  • Regular company and team bonding events.

  • Global volunteering and community initiatives

Our Benefits:

title: Senior Sales Engineer - Majors (UK/Nordics/Netherlands)
description:
As a Senior Enterprise Sales Engineer, you’ll serve as a trusted technical advisor and strategic partner to both customers and Sales. You’ll lead complex technical evaluations, align solutions to business outcomes, and help shape deal strategy in high-impact opportunities.

This role goes beyond delivering demos - you’ll own the evaluation experience end-to-end, influence key stakeholders, and help drive successful outcomes across enterprise accounts.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the technical strategy across your accounts as a peer to the Account Executive - a standing weekly 1:1 with each AE you support, and a standing weekly account team call with the full ecosystem where you carry POV status, technical blockers, and the explanation behind any usage movement.
  • Own the technical explanation behind consumption movement in your accounts. Work with the CSM and TAM to separate legitimate growth from misconfiguration, make sure legitimate growth gets quantified before renewal, and flag forward-looking usage the customer has signalled rather than explaining it backwards a month later.
  • Lead discovery in every meeting, not only in discovery meetings - including meetings where you were invited to present. Leave each meeting knowing something about their business you did not know going in.
  • Deliver engaging product demos, technical presentations, solution workshops, etc. that connect platform capabilities to customer outcomes for diverse stakeholder audiences including executives
  • Full ownership of the technical evaluations (POVs) end-to-end: scoping use cases and requirements, defining competitive success criteria, building a project plan with clear timelines, and holding all participants accountable to the process
  • Identify, develop, and leverage technical champions across multi-stakeholder environments, building a structured plan for champion cultivation and influence throughout the deal cycle and beyond
  • Contribute to product direction through active participation in structured product and engineering field feedback sessions, bringing field insights and customer patterns to PM and engineering teams
  • Drive operational excellence by ensuring activity, deal progress, and customer interactions are accurately documented and up to date in related systems
  • Identify and proactively resolve technical and organizational blockers by collaborating across Product, Support, and GTM teams before customers are impacted
  • Contribute to team enablement by mentoring peers, sharing best practices, and creating reusable assets that scale knowledge across the region

Who You Are:

  • 7+ years of experience in Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or a technical customer-facing role within an enterprise environment
  • Skilled at influencing and adapting communication across technical, business, and executive audiences
  • Advanced background in public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), Kubernetes, APM/tracing, security, developer experience, observability
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • Experience displacing or consolidating away from an entrenched incumbent inside an account where that incumbent has internal advocates
  • A consultative, outcome - oriented approach to problem-solving and customer engagement
  • Demonstrated depth over breadth. You have worked a very small number of very large organisations over long horizons, and can describe how your understanding of one account compounded across quarters.
  • Experience mentoring peers or contributing to team enablement initiatives
  • Demonstrated capability of utilizing AI tooling and scaling it
  • Growth mindset of embracing change and being curious
  • Willingness to travel as needed to support customer engagements

title: Staff Product Designer - Platform Design
description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

Spotify runs on the tools we've built for ourselves. They help hundreds of teams ship every day to hundreds of millions of people around the world. Now, we're sharing them.

Spotify Technology brings our proven tools and services together for engineering organisations everywhere, from global enterprises to individual developers. As AI reshapes how software gets made, we're building on years of experience solving complex engineering challenges at scale.

Platform Design makes these powerful tools feel effortless. We shape the services, products and experiences used by Spotify's engineering teams and by developers around the world. We believe great design is a competitive advantage, and developer tools deserve the same care and craft as any consumer product.

As a Staff Product Designer, you'll combine product leadership with hands-on design and engineering. You'll shape the experience strategy for a key part of the Spotify Technology portfolio, establish a distinctive visual language, and turn internal tools into products customers love using. You'll work closely with product, engineering and marketing partners, reporting to the Spotify Technology Design Director.

What You'll Do

  • Lead complex design challenges from early exploration through to production, creating intuitive flows, interfaces, interactions and motion that make powerful developer tools easier to use.
  • Shape the visual language of Spotify Technology, bringing consistency, personality and craft across product experiences and brand touchpoints.
  • Transform tools built for Spotify's engineering teams into compelling commercial products that meet the needs of developers and enterprise customers.
  • Bring design to life in code, building and shipping high-quality front-end experiences with close attention to performance, accessibility and detail.
  • Set experience strategy across your product area, partnering with product and engineering leaders to influence priorities, guide decisions and shape the roadmap.
  • Use prototypes, storytelling and experimentation to make complex ideas tangible, build alignment and help teams navigate trade-offs.
  • Explore how generative AI and agentic tools can improve design and development workflows, while creating thoughtful experiences for products used by people and AI agents.
  • Raise the bar for design craft across the team, championing design systems, inclusive experiences and a culture of collaboration, feedback and continuous learning.

Who You Are

  • You have a strong background in product design, with experience shaping complex digital products and delivering high-quality visual and interaction design.
  • You're comfortable working across strategy and execution, setting a clear product direction while staying close to the details of design and delivery.
  • You can build and ship user interfaces using a modern front-end technology stack, and enjoy bringing your designs into production.
  • You understand how to create cohesive visual experiences across product and brand, with a thoughtful approach to interaction, motion and design systems.
  • You bring an understanding of developer tools, enterprise software or platform products, including the challenges of designing for technical audiences.
  • You use generative AI and agentic tools in your work, applying sound judgement about where they add value and where human expertise matters most.
  • You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, using research, data and customer insights to make informed decisions and solve complex problems.
  • You communicate ideas clearly, build trust across disciplines and influence product decisions through compelling design work and storytelling.
  • You care about helping others grow, welcome different perspectives and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative environment where great work can happen.

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in London, UK or Stockholm, Sweden
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

description:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. We are seeking a strategic community management professional to join our International Community Team, and lead a growing team in EMEA. As the Manager of Community for EMEA, you will spearhead the development and execution of the community strategy that supports Reddit’s growth in the region.

In this role, you will lead a team of Community Specialists and will take charge of defining the roadmap for community activation and moderation across focus markets, and help develop our international playbook.

Your work will focus on experimenting, iterating, and refining processes that drive community engagement at scale. The insights you generate through these efforts will accelerate Reddit’s growth in EMEA, and serve as a model for other emerging markets. This role reports to the Director, International Community.

Responsibilities:

  • Craft and champion the regional community strategy, ensuring alignment with overall team and business goals.
  • Drive the iteration, innovation, and scaling of the community and moderator growth playbook, proactively identifying new opportunities and launching bold initiatives in key markets.
  • Inspire and empower regional teams to execute impactful programs that elevate local communities, and their markets. Encourage innovation and create an environment of continuous learning and improvement.
  • Recruit, onboard, and train local community specialists in key markets to strengthen our collaboration with moderators and drive community engagement.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Growth, Product, Engineering, etc.) to ensure successful alignment and execution of new initiatives.
  • Gather regional insights and learnings, and effectively report results to various internal stakeholders.
  • Lead, coach and develop the regional team; translate strategy into quarterly and sprint priorities, clear ownership and milestones; review risks and capacity, and unblock delivery
  • Own community-health and growth outcomes across priority markets, including KPI progression, moderator coverage and retention, and the impact of community-building initiatives.
  • Coordinate with Content, Growth, Product and relevant safety partners to deliver market initiatives and surface local needs for broader roadmap decisions.

Required qualifications:

  • 5-7 years of experience in community management or marketing operations, including at least 1-2 years in a leadership role, with a proven track record of driving community growth and delivering business impact through community-led or marketing projects.
  • Organized with a strong ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.
  • Problem-solver with excellent interpersonal skills, capable of collaborating with diverse cross-functional teams and influencing them to adopt a community-first mindset.
  • Comfortable testing, iterating, and adjusting strategies to find the optimal approach for each market.
  • Skilled at navigating ambiguous environments and experimenting with different approaches to achieve results in focus markets.
  • Data-driven and results-oriented, with a keen ability to translate insights into action.
  • Deep understanding of Reddit’s unique identity, and the critical role communities and moderators play in adding value to the platform and enhancing user experiences.

    • Experience in moderation on Reddit or similar platforms (e.g., Discord, Facebook, or other forums).

title: Trainer (Warehouse)
location: Barnsley, Yorkshire and the Humber, GB
description:
The Opportunity

Turn your industry experience into someone else’s opportunity. Join an established apprenticeship team within the Business and Warehousing area of Barnsley College Apprenticeships and help learners build the skills, knowledge and confidence to succeed in warehousing and supply chain careers. With long-standing relationships with key employers across Barnsley and South Yorkshire, you will join a team with strong foundations and a shared commitment to helping others achieve.

You will plan and deliver engaging, practical training, manage a caseload of apprentices and work closely with employers to connect learning with the workplace. From identifying starting points and creating individual training plans to assessing progress, monitoring off-the-job training and preparing learners for assessment, you will support apprentices throughout their journey. You will provide constructive feedback, keep accurate records using Aptem and work collaboratively with colleagues across departments to arrange additional support where needed.

You do not need to be an established teacher or assessor to bring something valuable to this role. Teaching and assessment training will be provided where needed, helping you turn your occupational expertise into a rewarding career developing others.

About You

You will bring extensive, relevant experience of the warehousing and supply chain sector, with up-to-date knowledge of industry processes and working practices. Just as importantly, you will enjoy sharing what you know: explaining ideas clearly, inspiring and motivating others, and helping people recognise what they can achieve. Whether you are an experienced trainer or an industry professional ready for a change, we would love to hear from you.

Well organised and proactive, you will be confident managing your own workload, building positive relationships with employers and working collaboratively across departments. You will adapt your approach to different learners, recognise when someone needs extra help and work with colleagues to put support in place. A passion for helping others, a flexible approach and a commitment to your own professional development are central to this opportunity.

title: Learning Support Assistant
description:
General - The Learning Support Assistant will:

Have an understanding of the broad range of Special Educational Needs (specific learning difficulties, complex learning difficulties, moderate learning difficulties, autistic spectrum disorder, emotional behavioural, mental health & social communication difficulties, ADHD) with reference to how this affects pupils’ learning

Work under the guidance of teaching / senior staff to implement agreed work programmes

Provide support for teaching staff across the school in an appropriate learning environment

Assist with the integration of pupils with special educational needs and/ or disabilities, supporting a small group or on an individual basis within the classroom or on a withdrawal basis

Be an integral part of the school, working in close partnership with all staff

To liaise sensitively and effectively with parents/carers as agreed with the teacher and participate in feedback sessions or meetings as directed

Pupils - The Learning Support Assistant should:

Assist with the teaching of pupils; whole class, small groups and individuals as directed

Help pupils to access learning activities through specialist support

Provide feedback to pupils in relation to progress and achievement

Monitor and evaluate pupils’ responses to learning activities through observation and planned recording of achievement against pre-determined learning objectives

Encourage pupils to interact and work co-operatively with others and engage all pupils in activities

Be aware of and support difference and ensure all pupils have equal access to opportunities to learn and develop

Implement local and national learning strategies e.g. literacy, numeracy, and make effective use of opportunities provided by other learning activities to support the development of relevant skills

Staff - The Learning Support Assistant should:

Assist the teacher in curriculum planning, management & preparation of resources

Be responsible for keeping and updating records as agreed with the teacher, contributing to reviews of systems/records as requested

Undertake marking of pupils’ work and accurately record achievement/progress

Implement agreed learning activities/teaching programmes, adjusting activities according to pupil responses/needs

Implement local and national learning strategies e.g. literacy, numeracy, early years and make effective use of opportunities provided by other learning activities to support the development of relevant skills

Support the use of ICT in learning activities and develop pupils’ competence and independence in its use

Specific Responsibilities of the Learning Support Assistant at St James’ Catholic High School

To work with the department and all staff in the promoting of inclusion of young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities

To support the learning of pupils with SEND

To be empathetic, highly supportive and understanding of the needs of individual pupils

To help pupils to access learning activities through specialist support

Administer and assess routine tests and invigilate exams/ tests

Be responsible for keeping and updating your own records in relation to your continued professional development

To attend training and development sessions

To work alongside the teacher to ensure that students achieve learning aims

To provide general clerical/admin support e.g. administer coursework, produce worksheets for agreed activities etc

To support charity work within school

To help to develop and maintain Individual Educational Plans (IEPs)

To be a presence in the classroom, where required

To attend SEND Departmental meetings

Other Specific Duties

Many specific responsibilities will require collaborative working with other team members which, as the Learning Support Assistant, you will develop proactively.

This post is subject to Enhanced DBS disclosure and basic online searches

Whilst every effort has been made to explain the main duties and responsibilities of the post, each individual task may not be identified. The post holder will be expected to comply with all reasonable requests from the Headteacher and SENCO to undertake work of a similar level that is not specified in their job description
